title: ready-03: sessions — palette `#` mode, CLI, plain `heca` attaches to the last one
summary: Named sessions, same-window # switching, GUI/CLI actions, explicit terminate/restart/delete with distinct client behavior.
description:
Third step of the server/client model. Depends on P099 (the connection). F012 accepted decision "Sessions: palette # mode, CLI flags, plain heca attaches to the last session, saved as JSON". Replaces the earlier plan of one process per instance with OS window switching.

## Goal
- The server holds many sessions, each with a name and a project folder (heca-pro stores its linked feature on it).
- **Palette `#` mode** beside `:` commands, `@` panes, `$` workspaces: one row per session (name, folder, windows attached, agents running); picking one switches this window; searchable and remembered.
- P100/T526 already delivered one palette mode table. Reuse it for # and preserve existing mode search history.
- Actions: new, rename, terminate, restart, delete, detach, switch — in the palette, bindable, callable by RPC.
- CLI (cli.rs flag style): `heca --sessions [--json]`, `--attach <name>`, `--new <name> [folder]`, `--kill <name>`, `--standalone`. Plain `heca`: server running → attach to the last session; none → start the server in the background, restore sessions, attach to the last. `--standalone` = today's behaviour.

## Preserve
- Text from wherever the app keeps user-facing text; nothing hard-coded. Not blocked by any other feature.

## Done when
- Two sessions; `#` in the palette lists both and switches in the same window; the CLI lists and attaches; plain `heca` reattaches to the last one.

## Approved Lifecycle (2026-10-27)
Canonical ownership: F012 decisions c205c5f5-cd0a-4212-9fda-8a8c63c98d3d and 2fc26220-2583-4392-bc2f-4724d406a555.
- Terminate stops processes and retains the session definition and stopped state. Clients remain open with Session unavailable and [Restart] [Exit].
- Restart is an explicit action. A terminated session must not restart just because a server or client reconnects.
- Delete stops it if active, removes Heca-owned runtime/selection references and closes its attached clients. Other sessions and project files are untouched.
- Normal GUI launch starts a missing server; existing disconnected windows show the agreed blocking server-unavailable dialog instead of restarting it automatically.
- --kill <name> is termination, not deletion; permanent-delete CLI spelling is still unspecified.
- T522 captures original launch executable/arguments/cwd and native harness session/driver identity. P105/T527 persists these and applies resume_programs=true / resume_harness=true through registered harness CLI capabilities.
- P100 owns live lifecycle and protocol. Persistence, durable deletion and restore after server exit belong to P105; they must not become a circular dependency that prevents T522 completing.

Additional acceptance: several clients observe the correct termination dialog; explicit restart targets the same session; deletion closes only that session's clients; stale references cannot recreate a deleted session. No T522 implementation or native acceptance is claimed yet.

Disabled resume does not remove or disable a pane: its own registered content starts fresh with its normal configured defaults. Terminal programs/harnesses become a normal shell, browser uses its default home, editor has no open files. This is generic for future registered content; T527 consumes existing managed-content factory/lifecycle ownership, without a closed content-kind list.

tasks.title: Sessions in the server: palette `#` mode, session actions, CLI, plain `heca` attaches to the last
tasks.description:
Execution task for P100 — read the phase and F012's decision "Sessions: palette # mode…" first. Depends on P099 (connection) and on the mode-table task in this phase (do that first). Replaces the old OS window-switching plan: no per-OS focus hand-over is needed any more.

Approved 2026-10-27 (F012 decisions c205c5f5-cd0a-4212-9fda-8a8c63c98d3d and 2fc26220-2583-4392-bc2f-4724d406a555):
- Keep distinct actions for terminate, restart and delete, alongside new, rename, detach and switch, through the existing catalog, GUI, bindings and RPC.
- Terminate stops session processes and retains its definition with a stopped state. Affected clients stay open with a blocking Session unavailable dialog and [Restart] [Exit]. Do not switch or restart automatically.
- Restart is explicit and rebuilds the retained session. Delete stops it if active, removes Heca-owned live references, and closes its attached clients. Do not delete project files or affect another session.
- --kill <name> is the planned terminate operation, not permanent deletion. It is not implemented yet. Permanent-delete CLI spelling remains unspecified; do not invent it.
- Capture original executable, structured arguments and working directory; retain registered harness driver identity and the native harness session ID. Never substitute a Heca session ID or PID.
- config.toml resume_programs=true and resume_harness=true are independent category defaults. P105/T527 owns durable JSON and policy-driven relaunch/resume through each harness's CLI API, not a universal --sessionId.
- Runtime lifecycle/state/launch capture belong here. Disk persistence, durable deletion and post-server-restart recovery belong to T527, which depends on this task; do not create a circular prerequisite.
- Preserve one socket/in-process code path, normal GUI auto-start of a missing server, same-window switching, other clients' attachment, and standalone behavior.

Edge cases: duplicate names; unknown attach gives a clear message and offers creation; last session terminated/deleted; several windows on one session; reconnect after server stop; terminated sessions never auto-resurrect. When resume is disabled, preserve the pane and initialize its own registered content's fresh default: a terminal-hosted program/harness becomes a normal shell; a browser uses its configured home page; an editor has no files open. This is an open factory/lifecycle contract for all future content, not a closed enum or a universal Terminal fallback. T527 consumes it; P094/T452 and P067/T398 retain ownership of the shared content factory foundations.

checklist.title: Server holds many sessions (name, project folder, free label for heca-pro)
Palette `#` mode: name, folder, windows attached, agents running; pick = switch this window
Actions: new, rename, terminate, restart, delete, detach, switch (GUI palette, key, RPC)
Plain GUI launch: attach last and start a missing server; T527 supplies disk restoration without a circular task dependency
Server unavailable: blocking Dialog with Close or GUI Restart and reconnect; no automatic restart by disconnected windows; reconnect to the intended session
Terminate retains a stopped session; its clients show Session unavailable [Restart] [Exit]; no automatic restart or switch; other sessions unaffected
Delete stops the session and removes Heca-owned live references; closes attached clients only, without deleting project files
Capture original executable, structured argv, cwd and native harness driver/session identity for T527 persistence

tasks.title: The palette's modes are declared once — one table read by both the sigil lookup and the palette
tasks.description:
T526: declare palette modes once (sigil, search scope and row source). Replace the duplicated sigil_for match and .mode calls in heca/src/chrome/palette.rs. Preserve mode= for action/RPC, query prefill, unknown-mode fallback and command/pane/workspace search history names. T522 owns real sessions.

Pre-flight 2026-10-15: reuse CommandPalette, Command, Input and SearchModel; app entries/pane_entries/workspace_entries, ActionCatalog, dispatch_intent. Searched docs/widgets.md, heca/src/components and chrome. No new widgets/tasks. Antonio confirmed no conflict with the other agent on these two files; split app palette (883 lines) and widget palette (1394) by responsibility in heca-f012 on feat/t526-palette-modes from origin/main. T468 remains with the other agent.

Plan: one app declaration per sigil/scope/rows source. Widget owns mode command assignment and named query prefill using its existing sigil table (no extra live mode state). Add a custom-mode regression, prefill/fallback/history checks; run scoped check, tests, Clippy and showcase. Baseline scoped cargo check passes.

Existing widget spacing constants and manual Input forwarding remain separate refactor scope; preserve these during the agreed file split.

---
**Completion summary:**
Implemented in /Users/antonio/projects/heca-f012 on feat/t526-palette-modes, based on origin/main e104bcc1. Changes are uncommitted and ready for Antonio's review.

App: heca/src/chrome/palette/modes.rs::MODES declares each sigil, durable search scope and pure row source once. populate registers that source through CommandPalette::mode_with_commands; the duplicated app sigil_for and row mode annotations are removed. heca/src/chrome/palette/mod.rs::open_command_palette uses the widget's query_in helper. The helper derives the prefix from the registered modes and sets the same query field that typed sigils use. Named prefill works before or after a mode declaration; direct edits, query replacement and closing clear builder input. Unknown names preserve the supplied query.

Split both oversized palette source files into component folders by responsibility. All 14 resulting source files are below 400 lines; largest is the 370-line app tests file. Public Command/CommandPalette import paths stay unchanged. Runtime rendering and the existing action policy/overlay dispatch remain in place.

Verified: 28 widget palette tests; 10 app palette tests including real RPC parse/catalog/action argument resolution and a custom row-source declaration; 3 native Rustdoc examples. Strict cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings passes, as do scoped cargo check, cargo doc -p heca-grid-ui -p heca --no-deps and git diff --check. Removing the shared sigil lookup deliberately makes the custom-mode regression fail; restored code passes.

Documentation: docs/widgets.md CommandPalette catalog, full builder tables, native and declarative examples, mode extension recipe; public Rustdoc in heca-grid-ui/src/widgets/command_palette/{mod,modes,command}.rs.

Verification limit: the compiled showcase launched, but Cua could not access its window (cgWindowNotFound), including through a temporary test bundle. Visual interaction remains unverified; both of our test processes were stopped. No real session mode was added; that remains T522. Existing spacing constants/manual off-tree Input handling remain the separately identified refactor scope. No new policy decisions. T468 and the other agent's source checkout were not edited. Review, commit and push await Antonio's instruction.

---
**Completion summary:**
Runtime review confirmed by Antonio: command and pane modes work; workspace selection switches correctly with both mouse and Enter. The earlier workspace-switching failure report was withdrawn. An empty query defaults to commands; ':' explicitly selects that same mode, as intended. No source changes were made during this investigation. Prior automated verification remains valid: 28 widget tests, 10 app tests, 3 Rustdoc examples, strict workspace Clippy, scoped cargo check and Rustdoc build. Work remains uncommitted in /Users/antonio/projects/heca-f012 on feat/t526-palette-modes, awaiting commit instructions.
